column5: API supplied HTML including seller authored product and store descriptions is rendered without any sanitisation
column6: The storefront renders API HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML in seven places and applies no sanitisation at any of them. HTMLRenderer at src/components/Functional/HTMLRenderer.tsx:10-16 passes its html prop straight through and is used for the product additional-detail block at src/components/Products/ProductDetailPage/AdditionalDetailSection.tsx:96 and for four CMS pages - about-us/index.tsx:67 - privacy-policy/index.tsx:67 - shipping-policy/index.tsx:47 and terms-and-conditions/index.tsx:72. Two further call sites inline the same pattern - src/components/Cards/PromoCard.tsx:83 renders promo.description and src/components/StoreProfile.tsx:154 renders store.description. No sanitisation library exists in the project at all - package.json has no DOMPurify or sanitize-html and a repo wide search for sanitize finds only the numeric input strippers in DepositModal and WithdrawModal. HyperCommerce is a MULTI SELLER marketplace per CLAUDE.md section 1 so product and store descriptions originate from sellers rather than from trusted staff. The storefront therefore depends entirely on the panel stripping active content on write - a dependency that is neither documented nor verifiable from this repository.
column10: A seller or content author able to store HTML in a product description - a store description or a promo description - and panel side sanitisation that is absent or incomplete.
column11: 1. Store markup containing an active payload such as an onerror attribute in a product description through whatever authoring path the panel provides. 2. Open the product detail page as a customer. 3. Observe whether the markup executes in the page origin.
column12: API supplied HTML is sanitised on render with an allow-list so stored markup cannot introduce script execution regardless of what reaches the database.
column13: The HTML is injected verbatim into the page so the storefront provides no defence of its own and the outcome depends entirely on panel behaviour.
column14: If panel sanitisation is missing or bypassable this is stored XSS on the most visited pages of the storefront. It compounds directly with issue 3 - no Content-Security-Policy and a JavaScript readable bearer token - and issue 14 - the same token in localStorage - so a single successful injection yields session theft rather than mere defacement.
column15: Sanitise on render with an allow-list inside HTMLRenderer and apply the same helper at the two inline call sites so there is one choke point. Treat this as defence in depth rather than a replacement for panel sanitisation - and confirm with the panel team what it strips on write so the two layers are documented rather than assumed.

column5: The 22 redesign sandbox routes and the design system page are publicly crawlable and indexable
column6: src/pages/redesign holds 22 route files and src/pages/design-system.tsx is a further one. None of the 23 emits a robots meta tag of its own - a search across src/pages/redesign and design-system.tsx for SEOHead - DynamicSEO - PageHead or next/head returns nothing - and public/robots.txt contains no Disallow entry for either path so both fall under the blanket Allow: / at the top of the file. Absence of a robots meta means indexable by default. Where a redesign page does inherit the default layout it is worse than neutral because SEOHead at src/SEO/SEOHead.tsx:53 emits a hard-coded index - follow with no prop to override it. These pages render the sandbox mock data from src/redesign/data/mock.ts rather than live catalogue data.
column10: Production deployment with the redesign routes present - which is the current state since the sandbox ships in the same build as the storefront.
column11: 1. Deploy the storefront. 2. Request /redesign/home/ or /design-system/ as a crawler with no referrer. 3. Check for a robots meta in the response and check public/robots.txt for a matching Disallow.
column12: Internal design sandbox routes are excluded from indexing - by a noindex meta or a robots.txt Disallow or by not shipping them in a production build at all.
column13: All 23 routes are served with no robots restriction and are eligible for indexing alongside the real storefront pages.
column14: Search engines can index 23 internal pages carrying mock product data and placeholder copy. They compete with the real category and product pages for the same terms - they expose unreleased design work publicly - and any that duplicate a live screen create genuine duplicate content against the page they were built to replace.
column15: Add Disallow entries for /redesign/ and /design-system/ to the robots.txt template that scripts/update-robots.mjs consumes and emit a noindex meta on those routes. The stronger fix is to exclude the sandbox from production builds entirely so the routes do not exist outside development.

column5: The generated sitemap advertises two routes that do not exist including one the project has formally deprecated
column6: The static route list in scripts/generate-sitemap.mjs:13-27 is hand maintained and has drifted from the real route tree. Two entries have no matching page. /delivery-zones/ at :18 is submitted with priority 0.6 although there is no src/pages/delivery-zones directory - and CLAUDE.md section 9.11 states the feature is deprecated product wide and must not be ported or flagged as a gap - so the sitemap is actively advertising a removed feature. /products/ at :20 is submitted with priority 0.9 although src/pages/products contains only the [slug] detail route and the search route with no index page - so the listing URL the sitemap treats as the highest priority catalogue entry point does not resolve. Verified by checking every static entry against the filesystem: the other eleven all have a matching page.
column10: Any production build - the sitemap is regenerated during npm run build and submitted through the Sitemap directive in robots.txt.
column11: 1. Run npm run build to regenerate public/sitemap.xml. 2. Read the entries for /delivery-zones/ and /products/. 3. Request both URLs and observe they do not resolve to a real page.
column12: Every URL in the sitemap resolves to a real page - a sitemap is a statement that these URLs are canonical and worth crawling.
column13: Two of the thirteen static entries point at routes that do not exist - one of them at the highest priority given to any catalogue URL.
column14: Crawl budget is spent on URLs that cannot resolve and repeated 404s from a submitted sitemap degrade the trust search engines place in the whole file. Advertising the deprecated delivery-zones path also contradicts an explicit project rule.
column15: Remove both entries from the static list. Better - derive the static routes from the actual pages directory during generation so the list cannot drift again - and add a build time assertion that every sitemap URL resolves to a page.
